card.title: How to Troubleshoot And Fix iPhone Random Restarts Using Panic Logs

source.title: How to Troubleshoot And Fix iPhone Random Restarts Using Panic Logs

claims.statement: Start random-restart work by testing with known-good parts, then read the panic-full log's missing sensor / Sensor Array value and use the model-specific page.

iPhone 12 and older Missing sensors: mic1 = charging port flex (SE 2020 may be the board), mic2 = power button flex, prs0 = charging port flex, tg0b = battery/connector/data line, ans2 = NAND related.

Generic iPhone 13+ Sensor Array bits listed: 0x20 charging circuit, 0x40 gas gauge, 0x41 battery data, 0xa1 battery sensor, 0xa9 battery data variant, 0x400 gyro, 0x800 charge port, 0x1000 proximity, 0x4000 battery sensor, 0x20000 gyro (14 Pro+), 0x40000 charge port (14 Pro+), 0x80000 proximity (14–17), 0x100000 power button, 0x200000 front sensor / wireless coil, 0x300000 USB-C (Pro), 0x400000 wireless coil, 0x500000 battery.
Third-party analysers (iDevice Panic Log Analyzer, PanicFull.com) only suggest causes; there is no official Apple mapping.

procedure: Look up the missing sensor or Sensor Array value on the model page.
Remember values combine as bit flags.
card.caveats: The 'universal' table conflicts with some model pages (e.g. 0x100000 is the charge port on iPhone 14 and prox on iPhone 15; this page also lists 0x10000 for the 14 Pro power button where the 14 Pro page says 0x100000). Prefer the model-specific card. Community-written Repair Wiki page, paraphrased; check the linked page (and its images) before acting on a reading.
